wininst.identity: CPython 2.5.6 distutils wininst-6.exe, 61440-byte x86 installer stub
wininst.provenance: SHA-256 and length exactly match the independently fetched upstream binary. Original download and .forage.json retained in scratch/stranded-f825-review/upstream/generic.
trace: CRT entry calls main at 0x404065. It obtains its executable path, maps its own file, then calls the configuration/archive parser at 0x4041b1.

0x4041df checks ZIP end-of-central-directory magic 0x06054b50; 0x4041eb checks the bdist_wininst config magic 0x1234567b. This standalone stub has no appended installation ZIP/config and ordinarily reports an invalid setup file.

The install path extracts files, maintains uninstall records/registry entries, locates the selected Python DLL and invokes Python install/byte-compilation scripts. At 0x402a15 it resolves PyRun_SimpleString via GetProcAddress; this is legitimate extensibility, not proof of a malicious script.
0x4027ca sets PYTHONHOME, loads the requested Python DLL, or looks up SOFTWARE\Python\PythonCore\%d.%d\InstallPath before loading it.

0x403749 writes an uninstall cleanup batch containing a delete/retry loop and launches it through CreateProcessA at 0x40381b, then resumes the child. 0x401187 restores extracted-file timestamps with SetFileTime.

These paths match the independently fetched CPython v2.5.6 PC/bdist_wininst/install.c. No packed or concealed hostile code was found. The member is vendored in a Jython-bearing JAR; the archive verdict is not inherited.
wininst.judgement_basis: Coherent installer behavior plus exact upstream bytes establish a legitimate bundled component. Installer execution, scripting, registry modification, deletion and timestamp changes remain notable. Deployment authorization and any separately appended packages are not supplied.
wininst.findings: No suspicious/hostile finding fires before or after. All existing observations remain except the inaccurately placed debug-marker union, whose two exact alternatives now have separate notable observations.

exporter_sfx.identity: WinRAR RAR5 SFX installing Windows Exporter 0.31.5 with NSSM 2.24-101-g897c7ad
trace: bsdtar extracts five RAR members: nodeExporterSrv.exe, windows_exporter.exe, private.key, certificate.pem and config.yml. 7zz lists the script but cannot decompress the newer RAR method; bsdtar successfully extracts the original bytes.
The SFX comment selects C:\Program Files\nodeExporterSrv and Setup=cmd /c nodeExporterSrv.exe install NodeExporterSRV with windows_exporter.exe and explicit monitoring arguments.

The configured server listens on :9100 at /baas-metrics with cpu,memory,logical_disk,net,tcp,udp,os,system collectors. config.yml selects TLS12, local certificate/key files and HTTP/2. It supplies no authentication stanza. No caller network or installation authorization is provided.

NSSM install dispatch reaches CreateServiceW at 0x14001347f with automatic-start type 2 and SERVICE_WIN32_OWN_PROCESS type 0x10; runtime service dispatch is at 0x14000a797 and configured-child CreateProcessW at 0x140013140. Lifecycle-hook creation is at 0x1400076ca.

Go main.main calls main.run at 0x140689ca6. run parses collector/configuration flags, constructs/enables collectors and registers HTTP handlers. The configuration exposes requested host monitoring counters; no credential-theft or remote-command chain is established.
windows_exporter.exe is byte-identical to the independently fetched official v0.31.5 amd64 release: SHA256 25dc64acbc5b4c23fded714fb9aea17b51a73ce39aa0db91c38dd78666ae208a, 22567864 bytes.
